discovery: The optical lattice clock and quantum-limited optical atomic timekeeping

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, trapping thousands of neutral atoms at a 'magic wavelength' where the trapping light leaves the clock transition unperturbed. This simple and general idea removes the conflict between strong confinement and spectroscopic accuracy. Ye and his group turned the concept into the most precise measurement devices ever built. They reached a fractional uncertainty below 10^-18, resolved the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample, and learned to control the collective quantum many-body interactions and spin-squeezed states that limit, and can now improve, the stability of the clock. Groups worldwide have adopted optical lattice clocks. They are driving the redefinition of the SI second, relativistic geodesy and searches for dark matter and for variation of the fundamental constants. They show how control of quantum measurement and dissipation turns fundamental physics into transformative technology.
